candidate_value.expression: (lambda n, k, l, d: any((lambda p: any((lambda path: all((path[j] <= path[j-1] + 1) and (path[j] <= n + 1) and (path[j] == n + 1 or (1 <= path[j] <= n and d[path[j]-1] + p[t % (2 * k)] <= l)) for j in range(1, len(path))) and path[-1] == n + 1)(path) for t in range(0, 2 * k) for path in [(0,) + tuple(range(1, n + 2))] if all(d[path[j]-1] + p[t % (2 * k)] <= l for j in range(1, len(path)))))(p) for p in [[0] + list(range(1, k + 1)) + list(range(k - 1, 0, -1))]))(*[int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()], *[int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[i+2].split()])
candidate_value.description: For each test case, the output is 'Yes' if there exists a sequence of positions and times where Koa starts at x=0 at time t=0, moves at most 1 meter per second or stays in place each second, and at every integer time t when she is at position x (1 ≤ x ≤ n), the depth d_x + p[t % (2 * k)] ≤ l, where p is the tide pattern [0, 1, ..., k-1, k, k-1, ..., 1] of length 2k. Otherwise, the output is 'No'.

confirmed_issues.instruction: The expression incorrectly assumes a fixed path (0, 1, ..., n+1) and checks it against all possible tide phases. This is not a valid approach because Koa can choose arbitrary waiting times at any position, and the path must be dynamically constructed to satisfy the depth constraint at each step. The expression must model the problem as a reachability problem where Koa can wait at any position (including the shore) for any number of seconds before moving forward, ensuring that at every integer time t when she is at position x (1 ≤ x ≤ n), the depth constraint is satisfied.
confirmed_issues.task_evidence: Koa can choose to stay on the shore for as long as she needs and neither the shore or the island are affected by the tide (they are solid ground and she won't drown there).
